string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and one of the country\'s four direct-administered municipalities. It is the nation\'s political, cultural, and educational centre. With a history spanning more than three thousand years, Beijing has served as the capital of several dynasties. The city is home to many landmarks including the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven, the Summer Palace, and sections of the Great Wall. Modern Beijing features a mix of historic hutongs and contemporary architecture. The city hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics and the 2022 Winter Olympics, making it the first city to host both. Beijing is a major transportation hub and a global city.

Shanghai is China\'s largest city by population and a major global financial centre. It is a direct-administered municipality on the eastern coast, at the mouth of the Yangtze River. Historically a small fishing village, Shanghai grew rapidly after it was opened to foreign trade in the nineteenth century. Today it is known for its skyline along the Huangpu River, including the Oriental Pearl Tower and the Shanghai Tower, one of the world\'s tallest buildings. The Bund showcases historic colonial-era architecture, while Pudong represents the modern financial district. Shanghai is a leading centre for commerce, culture, science, and technology.

Chongqing is a direct-administered municipality in southwestern China. It lies on the upper reaches of the Yangtze River and is known for its mountainous terrain and foggy climate. Chongqing is one of China\'s largest cities by area and population, covering a large region that includes both urban districts and surrounding rural counties. The city served as a wartime capital during the Second Sino-Japanese War. Chongqing is an important industrial and transportation centre, famous for its spicy Sichuan-style cuisine, particularly hotpot. Its dramatic hillside landscape and illuminated river views attract many visitors.

Tianjin is a direct-administered municipality in northern China, located on the coast of the Bohai Sea near Beijing. It is one of the country\'s largest port cities and an important gateway for maritime trade. Tianjin grew significantly in the nineteenth century when foreign concessions were established, leaving behind a distinctive collection of European-style architecture, particularly in the Five Great Avenues area. The city is a major manufacturing and logistics centre, and it is the northern terminus of the Grand Canal. Tianjin is known for cultural traditions such as clay figurines and kites.
